Article Title: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government
Article Text:

Air India pilots grounded till probe is over

NEW DELHI: The captain of Air India’s August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight, which experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet, was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival, whose result was “not negative” and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said Sunday.TOI had exclusively reported on Sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.The ministry has classified the incident, which led to 17 people being hospitalised, as serious and said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will probe it.“Further action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,” it said.Directorate General of Civil Aviation rules stipulate that “in case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety-sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received. In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisation” for de-addiction.Multiple passengers and cabin crew members on board the Airbus A320 operating as AI 2379 were injured when it suddenly lost altitude. The plane later landed safely in Delhi. “As standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing. Samples have been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,” the ministry statement added.Both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA, pending investigation.
Article Summary: The captain of air india’s august 4 phuket-delhi flight was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival. The result was “not negative” and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said sunday. Toi had exclusively reported on sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.

Article Title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
Article Text:
After bringing all crew members into the ‘citadel’, the master of the Golden Arsenal sought help from the Indian Navy, which responded swiftly to the distress call (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: On July 1, an attack by pirates on an India-bound bulk carrier, Golden Arsenal, in the Gulf of Aden was foiled after the captain moved all crew members, including an Indian seafarer, into the vessel’s “citadel” and sought assistance from the Indian Navy A citadel is a fortified safe room with essential supplies such as food and water, as well as communication equipment, where crew members can take refuge during a pirate attack. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel.Sharing this incident at the National Port Security Conference this week, Captain Vikram Singh Manhas, deputy nautical adviser at DGMA (maritime regulator), urged all crew members and masters to remain vigilant and follow preventive measures prescribed under best management practices (BMP), amid a rise in piracy incidents.Four vessels are held hostage by Somali pirates at present, three of which have Indian crew members aboard.One of the vessels has one Indian seafarer, while the other two have five and 11 Indian crew, respectively.Highlighting the significance of prevention in such cases, Manhas said that once a vessel is held by pirates, everything is dependent upon the negotiations with the pirates and that the government is working to ensure the safe release of Indian seafarers.In the direction of ensuring their safety, the government is set to launch a dashboard on August 15 to track every Indian seafarer on any ship. Additionally, shipping and ports minister Sarbananda Sonowal Saturday launched e-Samudra, a digital platform integrating services for seafarers, shipping companies, ports and other maritime stakeholders, and said, “Every Indian seafarer must be safe, respected and supported as India strengthens its position as a global maritime power. ”
Article Summary: After bringing all crew members into the ‘citadel’, the master of the golden arsenal sought help from the indian navy. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel. Four vessels are held hostage by somali pirates at present, three of which have indian crew members aboard.

Article Title: What's in a name? Pakistan boxer's hate for 'Narendra'

NEW DELHI: A Pakistani boxer who had "started hating" the name 'Narendra' after discovering that his Indian opponent, his coach and India's PM all shared the name drew laughs as Narendra Modi interacted with India's Commonwealth Games medallists Sunday.Boxer Narender Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him. Article Title: Captain of turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight may have failed dope test
Article Text:
The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet.

NEW DELHI: The captain operating Air India’s turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight on Tuesday (Aug 4) reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test conducted on arrival, according to multiple sources. The airline did not either confirm or deny it, saying while the tests were conducted, the results have not been shared with it.“We are aware that a post-flight screening test was conducted on the pilots in accordance with applicable protocols. However, the results of the test have not been shared with Air India, and we are therefore not in a position to comment on any findings,” an AI spokesperson said.“Air India undertakes regular drug testing of crew members in compliance with civil aviation regulations, independent of any specific flight or operational incident. We will continue to cooperate with the relevant authorities as required,” the airline added.The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. On arrival in Delhi, 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised. Sources say the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is probing this case from all angles including whether the handling of this turbulence event was correct; whether the event happened due to weather or some other reason; the likely impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.Pending probe, flight crew is taken off flying duty as per protocol. So the pilots of this flight are also not flying currently. DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such crew member can return for active duties with a negative dope test report.But after resuming flying if the same person tests positive for psychoactive substances again, their licence will be suspended for three years. And if after resuming flying the same person again tests positive for the third time, the flying licence is cancelled.International Civil Aviation Organisation says that “holders of licences shall not exercise the privileges of their licences and related ratings while under the influence of any psychoactive substance, which might render them unable to safely and properly exercise these privileges”.While the probe in Tuesday’s event would have focused on pilot handling the situation anyway, the captain reportedly testing positive adds another dimension to the same.
Article Summary: The captain operating air india’s turbulence-hit phuket-delhi flight reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test conducted on arrival. The airbus a320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised.

Article Title: Afghanistan qualify for 2027 ODI World Cup after thrilling win over Ireland
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Afghanistan secured direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup after beating Ireland by three wickets in the third ODI at the Civil Service Cricket Club in Belfast on Monday. The win also gave Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match series.Afghanistan bowled Ireland out for 206 in 46.3 overs before chasing down the target in 44.5 overs. The win was set up by a strong bowling effort and a calm finish from Rashid Khan.Afghanistan entered the third ODI knowing that a win would be enough to seal their place in the 2027 ODI World Cup. They had already beaten Ireland by 92 runs in the second ODI, while the opening match of the five-match series was washed out.Afghanistan looked in control at 97 for two during the chase but lost five wickets for 79 runs to slip to 176 for seven.Rashid then stepped up when his team needed him most. He remained unbeaten on 37 off 43 balls, hitting four boundaries, while Yamin Ahmadzai stayed not out on four off 26 balls.The pair held their nerve to take Afghanistan across the finish line without any further damage.Rashid was named Player of the Match for his crucial contribution.Afghanistan, currently ranked No. 8 in ODIs, have now secured direct qualification for the 2027 World Cup, which will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.This will be Afghanistan's fourth appearance in an ODI World Cup.Afghanistan captain Rahmat Shah credited his bowlers for sticking to their plans and adapting quickly to the conditions."Thank you. It was a low-scoring match, always tough. Finally, we won the match."On Afghanistan's bowling performance, he said: "Yeah, I give them the plans according to the field, according to the situation, and they read very well, especially Yamin Ahmadzai bowled really well, Rashid and Ghanzafar, they bowled really well too. They bowled according to the field, and especially they assessed the conditions early."Rahmat said Afghanistan's chase was challenging because of the low-scoring nature of the game."Of course, yes, because always a low-scoring match is very tough, and finally we won the match."He also pointed out the ninth-wicket partnership that helped Ireland post a competitive total and said Afghanistan would look to break such partnerships earlier in future."I think the ninth-wicket partnership, Ireland did very well. Inshallah, we try to break these partnerships early if we are in a good situation on that time. Inshallah, we will try our best."
Article Summary: Afghanistan secure direct qualification for the 2027 odi world cup after beating ireland by three wickets in the third odi. The win also gave afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match series. Afghanistan bowled ireland out for 206 in 46.3 overs before chasing down the target in 44.5 overs.

Article Title: 'Meri galti nahi thi': Harbhajan Singh reveals why he was expelled from NCA - WATCH

NEW DELHI: Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh has opened up about an incident that led to his expulsion from the National Cricket Academy (NCA) in Bengaluru in 2000.Harbhajan, who was among the first group of trainees at the NCA, recalled how he tore up a diet chart after repeatedly complaining that the food being served did not match the prescribed diet. He said the incident was later used as the reason for his removal.Harbhajan said the NCA had a fixed diet plan for its trainees, but the food served did not follow the chart. According to him, repeated complaints did not lead to any change.The former India spinner said his frustration eventually boiled over and he tore the diet chart."Waha se mujhe nikaal diya gaya. Woh meri galti nahi thi. Main aaj bhi is baat ko khule aam kehta hoon, kyunki woh hamara haq tha. Jo hamara khaana tha, woh achha nahi tha. [They removed me from there. It was not my mistake, I say this openly even today. It was our right. The food was not good there]," the former India spinner said on cricketnextofficial."Wahan jo rules aur regulations the, woh yahi the ki humein bahut kuch padhaya ja raha tha, sikhaya ja raha tha. Ek chart lagaya tha, jismein tha ki ye diet honi chahiye, expert ki diet ke hisaab se humein woh diet milni chahiye.Lekin woh khaana mil nahi raha tha. [Back then, the rules and regulations were such that we were told and taught a lot, and a chart was put up for the diet. But we were not getting food as per that diet. Despite complaining many times, the food did not improve. So one day I tore that chart. He also played 28 T20Is and took 25 wickets.

Article Title: Sarfaraz Khan's return: A 17kg weight loss, relentless fight and a Test recall
Article Text:
Sarfaraz Khan (AP Photo)

Shedding weight

Sarfaraz Khan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In cricket, as in life, fortunes can change in a short time. Over the years, Sarfaraz Khan has subtly expressed his frustration at being sidelined from the Indian Test team despite consistent performances in the Ranji Trophy On Friday, the Mumbai batter posted a photo on Instagram from the 2019 Telugu film ‘Jersey’ with a caption that read: “I may not fit in, but I’ll fight with everything I’ve got.”Just 48 hours later, the 28-yearold was rewarded for his seemingly endless ‘fight’ when he replaced the injured Sai Sudharsan in the Indian squad for the Test series against Sri Lanka. After finally receiving the news he had been waiting for, Sarfaraz shared his first post on social media, posting a couple of pictures in the Team India travelling jersey. On Monday, Sarfaraz was the cynosure of all eyes as he practiced with the Indian team in Colombo.On eve of Sarfaraz’s departure, Sarfaraz’s father-cum-coach Naushad Khan , who has a penchant for shayari when he’s not coaching his kids, posted a reel where he tells his cricketer sons Sarfaraz and Musheer Khan that luck favours hardwork.The Test recall, which has come after 19 months in the wilderness for Sarfaraz, marks a heartening comeback of a man who was last year ignored by the national selectors even for the India A home series against South Africa A ahead of the Proteas’ tour of India, based on the logic that they had “seen enough” of him and wanted to try the others too.With the three-day warm-up game in Colombo having concluded on Sunday, Sarfaraz will look to make the most of the practice sessions to prepare for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka.One of the criticisms against Sarfaraz was that he was overweight. Many deemed him unfit to play toplevel cricket, even though legendary opener Sunil Gavaskar countered that by saying that a player’s performance and cricket fitness are more important than their body weight. In a heartening development that has certainly helped him in his cricket career, Sarfaraz, before being picked for the India A squad for the upcoming tour of England last year, eventually decided to improve on this aspect too.After remaining unsold in the IPL for two years before the Chennai Super Kings bought him in IPL-2026 auction, he worked hard on improving his fitness in recent times, and shedding excess weight. The Mumbaikar has lost a staggering 17 kgs in a year’s time and now bears a much trimmer, fitter look. In fact, since 2025, Sarfaraz’s whole family has been on a weightlosing spree which has produced significant results. Advised to lose weight on an urgent basis to avoid a knee replacement surgery, Naushad Khan lost 12 kgs in a month last year.“Our whole family is focused on a weight-losing mission. Sarfaraz has lost nine kilograms too in six weeks, which isn’t easy, and he’s raring to lose more weight. Both Sarfaraz and I have been slogging in the gym for at least an hour for six days a week. I go for a walk, while he jogs for almost an hour, and then there’s a 30-minute swimming session. Even my younger son Moin (Khan) has lost a lot of weight,” Naushad had told TOI.Much of this weight loss mission for the Khans also involved a strict diet. “Sarfaraz and I have stopped eating atta (flour) and rice at home completely. Our diet is now strict but interesting — we eat sauteed vegetable with boiled chicken, boiled eggs, and drink green tea and black coffee. We are using little (olive) oil in our food,” Naushad had revealed.It meant that Sarfaaz was no longer feasting on his favourite non-vegetarian dishes — particularly biryani — but it’s a sacrifice that the middleorder batter consciously made to improve his fitness drastically.
Article Summary: Sarfaraz khan replaced the injured sai sudharsan in the indian squad for the test series against sri lanka. The test recall, which has come after 19 months in the wilderness for sarfaraz, marks a heartening comeback of a man who was last year ignored by the national selectors.

Article Title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' marriage keeps "breaking up" online, and it's never because of anything they actually did
Article Text:
Brittany Mahomes opens up about their marriage.(Image via Getty Images)

Why Patrick and Brittany Mahomes can't escape marriage trouble rumors, no matter what they do

"resting b***h face."

"Man people are weird... love you babe"

"sad how disrespectful some women are"

"not going to disturb my peace"

Why the "shut it down" strategy never actually works

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

There's a version of fame where nothing you do is neutral. Sit apart at a game, you're clearly divorcing. Sit together and smile, you're clearly overcompensating. That's the box Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have been stuck in for years now, and the latest round proves it hasn't gotten any less absurd or any less exhausting for two people who've been together since high school.At the FIFA World Cup quarterfinals on July 11, cameras panned to the Mahomes' luxury box at Arrowhead and caught something apparently scandalous: Patrick, seated a row behind Brittany, looking at his phone. That was it. That was the whole incident.Journalist Danilo Lacalle called it "weird" on X, another post joked "BREAKING: married couple gets into argument," and from there the algorithm did what it does. Someone else declared the body language "not happy marriage behavior," and a comparison to Donald and Melania Trump's famously frosty public dynamic started making the rounds too.What actually undercuts the panic, if anyone bothered to check: Patrick and Brittany had attended JuJu Smith-Schuster's wedding together just one day earlier, and by all accounts looked like they were having a great time. Nobody screenshotted that.If this were an isolated moment, it'd barely be worth writing about. It's not. The Mahomes' have been fending off "trouble in paradise" narratives for years, and the receipts pile up fast:Back in 2022, viral footage from a Texas Tech game showed Patrick saying something to Brittany that left her visibly stunned, prompting one X account to claim he'd told her to fix herPatrick addressed it obliquely on Twitter, saying,without ever confirming what was actually said.By 2024, actual body language analysts were being brought in by gossip outlets to dissect the couple's posture in red carpet clips, with one expert describing Patrick's reach for Brittany's hand as "stiff" and "obligatory" rather than affectionate, and reading Brittany's turned head as a sign she wanted distance. This is, to be clear, a professional interpreting a few seconds of hallway footage between two people who've been together for over a decade.There's also a persistent infidelity thread that never fully goes away. In 2023, Brittany addressed rumors about other women pursuing Patrick directly in an Instagram Q&A, calling itand insisting they werewhile admitting it used to bother her more than she let on. That admission, meant to shut the topic down, arguably kept it alive; it gave people a real quote to keep recirculating every time a new rumor cycle starts.Now, beyond the usual gossip churn, the Mahomes' have tried the obvious counter-move, repeatedly, and it never lands the way they'd want.Eight days after the World Cup seating drama, at the tournament final between Spain and Argentina, Brittany posted a run of Instagram Stories from their suite before kickoff, and the couple was photographed all smiles watching the match together. It read almost too clearly as a rebuttal. They ran the same play back at the F1 Miami Grand Prix in 2025, holding hands for the cameras in the middle of an earlier round of split chatter.The problem is the logic has no exit. Distant photos get read as evidence of a crack. Happy photos get read as evidence they're covering for the crack. A body language expert can find something "off" in either one if that's the assignment.There is no photo that proves a marriage is fine to an audience that's already decided otherwise, which means the "shut it down" strategy was never actually going to work, because it was never really about proof to begin with. It's about a couple famous enough that any unremarkable moment gets filled in with a plot.Patrick and Brittany started dating in high school in 2012, got engaged at Arrowhead in 2020 right after his first Super Bowl ring ceremony, married in Maui in 2022, and now have three kids together. That's over a decade of actual, verifiable history. Neither of them has directly addressed this latest round of speculation, or really any round before it, and at this point, that silence might be the closest thing to a tell we're going to get: not that something is wrong, but that they've stopped expecting a rumor mill this committed to being right to ever actually be talked out of it.
Article Summary: Patrick and brittany mahomes have been dogged by marriage rumors for years. At the world cup, cameras caught patrick mahomes looking at his phone. The couple has tried to shut down the rumors, but it doesn't work. There is no photo that proves a marriage is fine to an audience that's already decided otherwise.

Stephen Curry spent part of his offseason golfing with Jayson Tatum on Martha's Vineyard, and the outing was enough to send Boston Celtics trade speculation into overdrive. Unconfirmed reports placed the Warriors star on the course alongside Tatum, with former Celtic Brian Scalabrine possibly joining them, and fans wasted no time turning a quiet round of golf into a full recruiting pitch.No team has confirmed the meeting happened or connected it to any basketball business, but that detail barely slowed anyone down online.The sighting itself was simple, two of the NBA's biggest names sharing a golf course during the offseason relaxation. Scalabrine's possible presence added another Celtics thread to the story, even though nothing about the gathering pointed to anything beyond a social outing.That didn't stop the internet from filling in the blanks. Edited photos of Curry in Celtics colors spread quickly, along with imagined lineups pairing him with Tatum and Derrick White. For a fan base starved of offseason drama, one golf outing was more than enough fuel.Part of what kept the story alive is timing. Curry, at 38, is entering the stretch of his career where every offseason move gets read as a signal, and Golden State's recent seasons have left plenty of fans and analysts wondering how much longer this run lasts. A photo with Tatum, even an innocent one, landed on top of that uncertainty.Warriors fans pushed back hard on the fantasy scenarios, arguing Curry has represented Golden State for his entire career and isn't going anywhere.Others made the separate point that Tatum should remain the unquestioned face of Boston's roster regardless of who he plays golf with in July.There's also a real hypothetical buried under the noise. Trading for Curry would require Boston to navigate his $62.6 million salary, and the type of package that could theoretically get a deal done would have to lean on a big contract like Paul George's to match money, something the Celtics can't even attempt until September 6 under NBA aggregation rules. That's a lot of machinery for a story that started with a golf outing.The short answer, based on everything actually known right now, is no. Curry is expected to continue with Golden State and could become eligible for a two-year extension worth roughly $136.7 million, a deal that would keep him under contract through the 2028-29 season.He's also stated a personal goal of playing at least 20 NBA seasons, which requires him to stick around well past his current deal rather than chase a ring elsewhere. People close to the situation have maintained he has zero intention of requesting a trade, and Golden State's front office continues building its financial planning around keeping him as the franchise centerpiece.Until Curry or either organization says otherwise, the Martha's Vineyard photo belongs in the same bin as every other offseason golf sighting: a fun distraction, not a trade signal. Boston fans can keep building their fantasy roster. Golden State just isn't selling.
Article Summary: Stephen curry and jayson tatum met up on martha's vineyard. The outing was enough to send boston celtics trade speculation into overdrive. Curry is expected to continue with golden state and could become eligible for a two-year extension worth roughly $136.7 million.

Article Title: 'Creates uncertainty, disrupts planning': Associate nations take aim at ICC over ODI World Cup format changes
Article Text:
ICC chairperson Jay Shah (left), and Men's ODI World Cup trophy

Cricket Scotland and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association (KNCB) on Monday criticised the International Cricket Council’s recent changes to the qualification pathway and format for the Men’s 50-over World Cup.The two European Associate Member boards said they were disappointed that the ICC had made what they described as “significant structural changes” less than 18 months before the tournament."Cricket Scotland and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association (KNCB) are deeply disappointed by the International Cricket Council's recent decision to implement significant structural changes to the ICC Men's 50-over World Cup qualification pathway and tournament format with less than 18 months until the competition begins," the two boards said in a joint statement.The ICC announced the changes in June as part of a revamp of the structures for its two men's World Cup tournaments. The changes include the introduction of 'Super Series' and 'Super 7' rounds at next year's 50-over World Cup.The tournament will still have 14 teams, as previously planned. However, the three lowest-ranked teams will now first play in a 'Super Series' round. Only the team that finishes top of that round will advance to the main 12-team group stage.From the main group phase, the top three teams from each group, along with the next best-placed team across the two groups, will advance to the new 'Super 7' round.Scotland and the Netherlands said the changes could affect the growth of Associate Member cricket."These changes represent a setback to Associate Member cricket and risk undermining the progress made in recent years to grow the global game."They also questioned the timing and consultation process behind the changes."Decisions of this significance, particularly those directly affecting Associate Members, should be made clearly following meaningful consultation and with sufficient notice for affected Members to understand and respond to the implications. The timing of these changes, with less than eighteen months until the tournament, has given affected Members limited opportunity to contribute to the process or adapt. We believe greater engagement with Associate Members would have supported a more effective and collaborative approach and help maintain confidence in the qualification pathway," the joint statement added.The two boards said changing qualification rules during a cycle creates uncertainty for players and teams."Members and their players invest years in preparing for World Cups, and confidence in those pathways depends on them not changing part-way through a qualification cycle without consultation. Changing those structures at short notice creates significant uncertainty, disrupts planning, and places additional operational and financial pressure on organisations that are already operating with limited resources," the statement further said.They also highlighted the importance of World Cup participation for Associate Members."The opportunity to compete at a World Cup provides Associate Members with a unique competitive opportunity to drive investment, inspire players, attract commercial partners and government support, and create moments that capture the imagination of supporters. Some of the most memorable moments in ICC tournaments have come when Associate Members have challenged, and in some cases defeated, Full Members on the world stage. Those performances have always reinforced the principle that success is earned on the field. Our players work incredibly hard with limited resources to earn these opportunities and deserve respect and for their efforts to be rewarded."The boards said providing Associate Members with opportunities to qualify for major tournaments was important if cricket wanted to expand globally."Leaders in cricket have consistently spoken about their ambition for the sport to become truly global. Providing meaningful opportunities for emerging nations to qualify for and compete at major events is fundamental to achieving that ambition. Decisions that reduce or limit those opportunities slow the progress being made to expand the game's reach and appeal and runs counter to those ambitions," it added.
Article Summary: The icc announced the changes in june as part of a revamp of the structures for its two men's world cup tournaments. The changes include the introduction of 'super series' and 'super 7' rounds at next year's 50-over world cup. Scotland and the netherlands said the changes could affect the growth of associate member cricket.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in glasgow. Prime minister narendra modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds. The prime minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements.

Article Title: Imported machines, non-toxic gel, double-door entries and monkey whisperers: How Delhi is bracing for BWF World Championships
Article Text:
The Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium will host the BWF World Championships from August 17 in New Delhi. (Image: TimesofIndia.com)

New Delhi:

Machines from the US have been brought in to tackle pigeons during the BWF World Championships in New Delhi. (Image: TimesofIndia.com)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Glass doors have been installed at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi as part of the infrastructural overhaul. (Image: TimesofIndia.com)

The Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi has received a fresh coat of paint, new infrastructure, and swanky lights ahead of the BWF World Championships , which return to India after a 17-year gap. The objective is to host the best in world badminton, administrators from around the planet, thousands of fans and multiple VIPs starting August 17. The objective is also to ensure the pigeons and monkeys stay away, avoiding a repeat of the chaos at the India Open, earlier this year.In January, during the India Open, pigeons halted play in the match between HS Prannoy and Loh Kean Yew. Denmark's Mia Blichfeldt strongly criticised the practice and warm-up facility's hygiene. She complained about dirty areas and bird droppings near the training courts.While the Badminton Association of India (BAI) refuted the allegations, they and the Sports Authority of India (SAI), alongside the Sports Ministry, are leaving no stone unturned in ensuring something similar doesn't happen again.Wooden doors have given way to a double-door entry system in order to keep the monkeys away from entering the four-court premises and the training facilities at the KD Jadhav Stadium. Vents have been sealed to keep the pigeons from entering. Additionally, six plug-and-play machines have been imported from the US and installed to emit noise made by predatory birds. Further, non-toxic gel has also been filled in the roof ducts.The wheels for the preparations began as early as February, with things picking up pace in May. Hundreds of workers and contractors from the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) have been busy at work for the past few weeks to bring the tournament to fruition."The order for the pigeon gel went out in April, and it was imported only recently; it arrives in 10 days. It is a plug-and-play machine and can be imported from one stadium to another," said a source tracking developments to TimesofIndia.com."The only hiccup is that it can't be used at one place for a long period. The pigeons get accustomed to it and understand that this is not natural. But in the last 15-20 days of tests, it has worked well," he added.The gel in use is castor oil-based and has been installed on the surface of the root at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. Every time a bird sits on the top of the arena, it'll slip, ensuring they stay away.Another challenge for the organisers in the past has been monkeys. A full-grown rhesus macaque roamed the upper tier of the stands during the India Open. Now, as part of a Rs 20 crore revamp, 16 entrances have been fitted with glass doors and an automatic double-entry system.And if all else fails, a four-man team, led by Delhi-native Jabbar, is on hand to make noises similar to that of a langur to fend off monkeys. Born into a family of professional monkey whisperers, Jabbar, who earns Rs 25,000 a month, is confident that his and his team's vocal cords will be enough to keep monkeys at bay.
Article Summary: The indira gandhi indoor stadium in new delhi has received a fresh coat of paint, new infrastructure, and swanky lights. The objective is to host the best in world badminton, administrators from around the planet, thousands of fans and multiple vips starting august 17.

Article Title: Stefon Diggs' fresh start takes an ugly turn after devastating Commanders injury
Article Text:
Stefon Diggs is a father of six children in 2026 (Getty Images)

Stefon Diggs gave the Commanders hope; Laremy Tunsil's triceps took it away.

The low: Tunsil goes down, and it's not minor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A team that can't seem to get a full deck

For exactly three days, everything about the Washington Commanders' offseason made sense. They'd landed a genuine No. 2 receiver, Jayden Daniels finally had real weapons around him, and the vibes across training camp were as good as they'd been all summer. Then Saturday practice happened, and the whole storyline flipped.Diggs' free agency saga had dragged for months. The Patriots released him in March purely for cap relief, even though he'd just led their receiving corps to a Super Bowl appearance. Washington waited him out, and on August 5, it paid off.Diggs signed a one-year deal worth up to $12 million, and the team made it official two days later. For a guy from Gaithersburg, Maryland, it was framed as him coming home, and for the Commanders, it was framed as exactly the piece missing next to Terry McLaurin.Behind those two, the depth chart had been thin: Treylon Burks, Luke McCaffrey, a rookie. Diggs instantly became the best receiver not named McLaurin on the roster, and gave Daniels a second real threat defenses actually had to respect.For a team that went 12-5 with an NFC Championship run in 2024, then collapsed to 5-12 in 2025 largely because of injuries, the Diggs deal read like exactly the kind of aggressive, no-nonsense move that had defined Washington's whole offseason approach.Add it to trading for left tackle Laremy Tunsil back in March 2025, and this looked like a front office building something real.Then Saturday came. During a one-on-one pass rush rep against Odafe Oweh, Tunsil tried to stop a bull rush, the two locked up, and Tunsil awkwardly disengaged, immediately grabbing his arm in obvious pain.The diagnosis: a torn triceps. He'll need surgery, and the recovery window for that injury typically runs four to seven months, meaning Washington's best offensive lineman, a five-time Pro Bowler who'd just become the NFL's first $30-million-a-year tackle five months earlier, is likely out for most, if not all, of the 2026 season.The timing is almost cruel. Tunsil was PFF's sixth-ranked tackle in the league last year, allowing just two sacks and 15 pressures the entire season. He was the only Commander named to ESPN's top-10 players survey heading into this year. And he was supposed to be the guy keeping Daniels upright after a 2025 season where Daniels himself missed 10 games to three separate injuries.Washington's internal options to replace him aren't great. Andrew Wylie has played almost exclusively right tackle for his whole career. Brandon Coleman, who'd been competing for a starting guard spot, is the most likely candidate to slide out to tackle; he started 12 games there back in 2024, so it's not unfamiliar territory, but it's also not Tunsil.So here's where the Commanders sit: a receiving corps that looks genuinely dangerous for the first time in years, and an offensive line that just lost its best piece before the season's even started. One signing bought them a week of optimism. One practice rep took it right back.
Article Summary: Stefon diggs signed a one-year deal worth up to $12 million with the washington commanders. The patriots released him in march purely for cap relief. Diggs instantly became the best receiver not named terry mclaurin. Tunsil was pff's sixth-ranked tackle in the league last year.

Article Title: Indian-origin teenagers Bodhana Sivanandan and Shreyas Royal become 2026 British chess champions
Article Text:
Bodhana Sivanandan and Shreyas Royal

Shreyas Royal won British Championship in open category

Indian-origin teenagers Bodhana Sivanandan and Shreyas Royal have made a major mark on British chess after winning the women’s and open titles at the 2026 British Chess Championships in Coventry.Bodhana, just 11, became the youngest-ever British women’s champion after beating 14-year-old Ireland-based talent Trisha Kanyamarala in a tense rapid-chess playoff.Her performance drew huge praise, with Grandmaster Danny Gormally saying: "Unreal! Bodhana has won. She is unbelievable, a generational talent," during his commentary for the English Chess Federation.Bodhana’s chess journey began during the COVID-19 lockdown, when a family friend gave her a chess board while returning to India. “I was interested in the pieces, so I started playing," she said at the time.Since then, the north-west London schoolgirl has collected major honours, including the UK Open Women’s Blitz title and a share of the British Women’s Rapid crown.Seventeen-year-old Shreyas Royal won the Open British Championship after finishing half a point ahead of England’s experienced grandmasters following nine rounds. It is his first British title and another major step in his rise as a top young chess player.Royal, who moved from Bangalore to the UK with his family at the age of three, became England’s youngest grandmaster at 15.His latest victory also attracted praise from former minister Sajid Javid, who recalled helping Royal’s family remain in Britain.“In 2018, as Home Secretary, I took a decision to allow Shreyas and his family to remain in the UK. Wonderful to see his extraordinary talent flourish. Britain is proud of you, Shreyas," he said.The 2026 championships featured more than 1,750 entries and a record £34,000 prize fund for the open event.

Article Title: Can Keely Hodgkinson become the first British woman to achieve European 800m hat-trick in European Athletics Championships following Olympics glory?
Article Text:
Keely Hodgkinson (via Getty)

Keely Hodgkinson eyes historic third European title ahead of European Athletics Championships in Birmingham

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Keely Hodgkinson is aiming to make history at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. The British Olympic champion is chasing a third consecutive European 800m gold medal. If she succeeds, she would become the first British woman to win the same individual event three times at the European Championships.Hodgkinson has already won European titles in 2022 and 2024. Now, she faces a strong challenge from Swiss star Audrey Werro and Dutch athlete Femke Bol . Despite her Olympic success, Hodgkinson insists the chance to win gold in front of a home crowd would be just as special as her triumph in Paris.The women’s 800m is expected to be one of the biggest races of the championships. Keely Hodgkinson enters the competition as the reigning Olympic champion. However, she will not have everything her own way.Werro has emerged as one of the biggest threats to Hodgkinson. The Swiss runner stunned Hodgkinson at the Stockholm Diamond League meeting in June. Werro won the race in 1:53.98, while Hodgkinson set a British record of 1:54.33.Werro then improved her personal best again in Paris three weeks later. She clocked 1:53.80 and strengthened her position as one of the leading 800m runners in the world.Hodgkinson, however, is not treating her Stockholm defeat as a setback. She believes the race showed how quickly the competition in the event is developing.The British star told Athletics Weekly that she is excited by the challenge and feels ready to compete. She admitted that June and July had been difficult at times, but added that she now feels in a strong place.Hodgkinson also pointed out that her Stockholm performance was still the fastest race of her career. She improved the British record by 0.28 seconds and believes that achievement should not be overlooked simply because she finished second.The 24-year-old also knows that championship racing can produce unexpected results. She recalled entering the Tokyo Olympics as the eighth-ranked athlete and leaving with a silver medal. On other occasions, she had started as the favourite but failed to win.That experience has taught Hodgkinson to approach major championships as a fresh challenge. She believes rankings and previous results do not always decide what happens on the track.A third European title would carry huge significance for the British runner. Hodgkinson said having her family in the stands and potentially hearing the British national anthem at a home championship would make the moment extremely special.She considers a European title almost as valuable as her Olympic success in Paris. For now, though, her focus remains on executing her own race rather than worrying about her rivals.The 800m heats are scheduled for Tuesday, with the semi-finals on Thursday. The final will take place on Friday evening.With Hodgkinson, Werro and Bol all in strong form, the women’s 800m could become one of the defining races of the Birmingham championships.
Article Summary: Keely hodgkinson aiming to make history at european athletics championships. The british olympic champion is chasing a third consecutive european 800m gold medal. If she succeeds, she would become the first british woman to win the same individual event three times at the european championships.
